chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Barqī, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, he said:

I asked him about a man who is in his house praying, while he thinks that night still remains upon him. Then another person enters through the door and says: 'Morning has come upon you.' Should he pray the witr or not, or should he repeat anything from the night prayer? He said: 'He repeats it if he performed it in the morning.'

The meaning in this report is that he only made repetition obligatory upon him if he performed it in the morning, because once morning begins, the time of the obligatory prayer has become constrained, so it is not permissible for him to perform a supererogatory prayer. Thus, if he performed it, it would be upon him to repeat it, because he performed it outside its proper time, as we have explained; that clarifies it.

key_terms.الْإِعَادَةَ: repetition of the prayer due to invalid timing
key_terms.الْوِتْرَ: the witr prayer, the concluding unit of the night prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed before dawn
key_terms.مُصْبِحًا: in the state of having entered morning, after dawn has come
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the time of the obligatory prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs ṣalāt al-layl thinking it is still night, then discovers dawn has already entered?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who was performing the night prayer thinking that night remained, only to learn that dawn had already entered. It indicates that if the prayer was performed after morning had begun, it must be repeated, because the time of the obligatory prayer has become restricted and voluntary prayer is no longer to be performed then.
